title: Affine charts along finite surjections with injective section maps
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] with structure morphisms $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $b:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $q:X\to Z$ satisfy $bq=a$. Assume $a$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $q$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], and for every affine open $V\subseteq Z$ the pullback $q^\sharp_V:\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)\to\Gamma(q^{-1}V,\mathcal O_X)$ is injective. Then $X$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, meaning every open cover has a finite subcover), and $Z$ admits a finite affine open cover $Z=\bigcup_j V_j$. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Z$, the inverse image $q^{-1}V$ is affine, with coordinate ring $B$, and $q^\sharp_V$ identifies $A$ with a $k$-subalgebra of $B$; $B$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and is finitely generated as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The ring $A$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra and is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The empty schemes and the empty affine cover are included.

source.place: Tag 00IS, lemma-Artin-Tate; agent-formulated affine-chart assembly of the retained item proof steps 1--2. The scheme and Noetherian inputs are the affine-pair finite-type characterization and finite-type-over-Noetherian results, detailed with their tags in report.md.

proof.text: Because $a$ is of finite type, it is quasi-compact and locally of finite type. The inverse image of the whole affine $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $X$, so $X$ is quasi-compact. Choose a finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_i W_i$. The affine-pair characterization applied to $a$, $W_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ says that each $\Gamma(W_i,\mathcal O_X)$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra.

source.place: Tags 01T1 (definition-finite-type) and 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize); the finite cover is the finite-subcover argument.

proof.text: Each of these coordinate rings is Noetherian by the finite-type affine algebra lemma. This affine cover proves that $X$ is locally Noetherian by its definition. Together with the quasi-compactness from step 1 this is precisely the asserted Noetherianity of $X$. If $X$ is empty use the empty cover.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), proof, together with properties.tex Tag 01OV (definition-noetherian).

proof.text: For any open cover $Z=\bigcup_\alpha O_\alpha$, continuity of $q$ gives an open cover $X=\bigcup_\alpha q^{-1}O_\alpha$. Quasi-compactness supplies finitely many indices. Their $O_\alpha$ cover $Z$: given $z$, choose $x$ with $q(x)=z$ by surjectivity, then use the chosen cover of $X$. Thus $Z$ is quasi-compact. This argument includes the empty cover when $X=\varnothing$, since surjectivity then forces $Z=\varnothing$.

source.place: Agent-written open-cover argument using surjectivity and continuity; no descent theorem is invoked.

proof.text: Apply the finite affine cover lemma to the quasi-compact open $Z$ of itself to obtain $Z=\bigcup_j V_j$ with finitely many affine opens. For an arbitrary affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Z$, finiteness of $q$ means directly that $U=q^{-1}V$ is affine, say with coordinate ring $B$, and that $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module via $q^\sharp_V$. The affine-pair characterization for $a$, $U$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives finite type of $B$ over $k$.

The relation $bq=a$ makes $q^\sharp_V:A\to B$ a $k$-algebra map. Its assumed injectivity identifies $A$ with its image $T\subseteq B$ as a $k$-subalgebra. If $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ generate $B$ over $A$, their same expressions generate it over $T$: replace each coefficient $c$ by $q^\sharp_V(c)$. A field is Noetherian, since an ideal containing a nonzero $c$ contains $c^{-1}c=1$ and otherwise is zero. Apply Artin--Tate with base $k$, ambient algebra $B$ and subalgebra $T$: $T$ is finite type over $k$. Lift its finitely many algebra generators through the bijection $A\to T$; injectivity then shows that they generate $A$ over $k$.

source.place: Tag 00IS (lemma-Artin-Tate), with the explicit elementary image-subalgebra identification.

proof.text: Apply the finite-type affine algebra lemma to $A$ over $k$ to conclude that $A$ is Noetherian. Since $V$ was arbitrary, every asserted chart has all the stated properties. For $V=\varnothing$, both coordinate rings are zero rings; the empty generating sets and the same Artin--Tate theorem apply, which requires neither the ambient algebra nor its subalgebra to be nonzero.
